newsitem.title: JAPAN: Oil spill delays Japan utility maintenance checks.
newsitem.headline: Oil spill delays Japan utility maintenance checks.

text.p: A Japanese power utility said on Tuesday it had delayed maintenance checks at two of its thermal power generators in case operation of nuclear reactors it owns along the Sea of Japan coast was hampered by oil slicks.
Kansai Electric Power Co Inc said chances that slicks from an oil spill would affect operation of its nuclear plants were slim, but it was taking precautions.
If the nuclear reactors were affected it would need the output from the thermal reactors.

Operation of Kansai Electric's three nuclear power plants -- Ohi, Takahama and Mihama -- along the Sea of Japan coast, has been threatened by an oil spill from a Russian tanker that broke up in rough seas on January 2.
The 13,157-tonne Nakhodka was carrying 19,000 tonnes (133,000 barrels) of fuel oil.
The nuclear reactors use seawater as a coolant, and large quantities of oil could clog up pipes that circulate the water.

Kansai Electric's 250,000 kilowatt (kw) Sakaikou No. 3 generator had been due to close for maintenance checks from January 20 to February 11, and its 450,000 kw No. 1 Kainan power generator from January 22 to February 1, a company spokesman said.
Turnarounds usually take about a month, he said.
